title: Albania's student protests
dek: Students join months of protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama's government, the riots and arrests in Tirana, and the competing accounts of who is behind the violence.
summary: Protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama's government began in late May 2026 over a luxury resort planned near the village of Zvërnec, beside a protected wetland on the southern coast. The project is backed by Jared Kushner, the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump. The movement, known as the Flamingo Revolution, held mostly peaceful rallies for months and widened into calls for Rama to resign over alleged corruption.

In mid-October university students joined, protesting fees, run-down universities and dormitories, and poor job prospects. From October 13 protests in Tirana turned violent: the Education Ministry, the prime minister's office, other government buildings and bank branches were set on fire, and police used tear gas and water cannon. Protests spread to Elbasan, Shkodër, Korçë and Lezhë. Police say 152 people were arrested over three days. The interior minister says 156 people were injured over four days, including 97 police officers and 45 protesters.

Rama says governments change through elections and will not resign. He blames "foreign hands" and the opposition for the violence; opposition leader Sali Berisha rejects that and backs the call for Rama to go. Students say months of peaceful protest were ignored. President Bajram Begaj and the EU delegation have urged calm and a proportionate police response.

Violence continued into the weekend. On Monday, October 19, protesters attacked the Appeals Tribunal, a day after a police station and the interior ministry's entrance were set on fire and windows were smashed at the ruling Socialist Party's headquarters. Rama said demonstrators had crossed a "red line", offered frontline police a bonus and pay rise, and again blamed "foreign hands", this time naming Iran and Russia. The European Commission condemned the violence and called for a proportionate police response.

ground.shows: Rama speaking from the fire-damaged College of Europe building near his office, accusing the opposition of using masked people and rejecting calls to resign.

phases.name: Protests spread; Rama refuses to resign

events.label: reported
events.text: Protests called by opposition Democratic Party leader Sali Berisha turn violent in Tirana; at least 13 people are arrested. Protesters want Rama and Deputy Prime Minister Belinda Balluku, whom prosecutors accuse of interfering in public contracts, to leave office. Rama later dismissed Balluku, Reuters reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: In late May, demonstrators try to block construction of a resort near Zvërnec, beside the protected Vjosa wetlands. Protests soon spread to Tirana and other cities, and the movement becomes known as the Flamingo Revolution.

events.label: reported
events.text: Thousands march in Tirana in the largest protest yet against the Kushner-backed resort, chanting outside Rama's office. Rama tells Reuters the project will go ahead and be completed responsibly; protesters say it lacks transparency.

events.label: reported
events.text: Rama calls the protests genuine but says foreign groups with anti-American and antisemitic views are trying to use them against Albania's interests.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Students protesting university conditions, fees and job prospects rally outside the Education Ministry in Tirana. The protest turns violent: stones are thrown, fires are set at the city hall and on Durrës Street, and police use tear gas and water cannon.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Police say protesters broke into the Education Ministry overnight and set a fire inside. Police report 16 arrests, 49 people facing criminal proceedings and six officers injured.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Riots last more than eight hours. The prime minister's office, ministry buildings and bank branches are set alight, and protesters build barricades. The Albanian media report protests at universities in Elbasan and Shkodër.

events.label: reported
events.text: Authorities say 23 police officers and six other people are being treated for injuries and 35 people have been detained, AP reports.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: President Bajram Begaj condemns the violence and calls for restraint from young people and proportionate force from police. Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu says protest is a right but no excuse for violence. The EU delegation expresses concern and calls for a proportionate response.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Rama tells Reuters that governments change through elections, not revolution, and says he will not resign, citing his mandate to complete EU membership talks. He says he is open to discussing education costs.

events.label: reported
events.text: Protests in Tirana become a riot again, with windows smashed and a bank raided. Police say 160 people were detained that evening over alleged violent acts.

events.label: disputed
events.text: Rama says the unrest is "not a student phenomenon" and blames "foreign hands"; he also accuses the opposition of using masked people. Opposition leader Sali Berisha rejects claims that the opposition is behind the violence and backs the call for Rama to resign.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Thousands march in Tirana on a fourth day, with clashes outside the Education Ministry. Protests are reported in Lezhë, Elbasan, Shkodër and Korçë. Rama writes on Facebook that the government will not bow to violence.

events.label: reported
events.text: Police say 152 people have been arrested over three days and 324 are under investigation, and that 71 officers have been injured. Students are boycotting classes and say they will not negotiate except on Rama's resignation.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: State Police chief Skënder Hita suspends two officers after videos appeared to show them using force on a protester lying on the ground, saying the force used was disproportionate, and orders a disciplinary investigation. Interior Minister Ervin Demo welcomes the move.

events.label: reported
events.text: Interior Minister Ervin Demo says 156 people have been injured over four days, including 97 police officers and 45 protesters, and urges parents to keep children away from the violence.

events.label: reported
events.text: Ombudsman Endri Shabani says his anti-torture team contacted 214 detained people in 72 hours, received complaints of police violence, found signs of violence on 26, and found minors questioned without a psychologist. No police response has been reported yet.

events.label: reported
events.text: According to AFP, police say 10 people were arrested after Friday's protests and criminal proceedings were opened against 22 more; the health ministry says 25 people, including nine police officers, suffered minor injuries in Tirana, Vlora and Lezha.

events.label: reported
events.text: Reuters, citing police figures, reports that about 500 protesters have been detained this week, 330 of whom have since been released, and that about 120 police officers and 45 protesters have been injured; it says protester injuries are likely under-recorded. Independent MP Marjana Koceku joins the call for Rama to step down.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Clashes continue for a fifth day as protesters gather outside the Education Ministry in Tirana; Reuters and AFP report rocks thrown at police, who use tear gas and water cannon. Rama says on Facebook that the government respects the students and will protect their right to protest, but will not let anyone jeopardise the country's future.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Several Albanian outlets report that police fire rubber bullets at protesters outside the Education Ministry; protesters say some people were hit. State Police chief Skënder Hita says only certified, permitted means were used, in a limited way, and urges parents not to let minors join the protests.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In the afternoon clashes move to the prime minister's office, where police use tear gas and water cannon and protesters throw stones. Koha Jonë reports three protesters taken to hospital, all conscious.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Rama launches "Dëmi im" ("My damage"), a scheme on the e-Albania portal for small businesses damaged in the protests to claim compensation, with tax teams to verify claims.

events.label: reported
events.text: Opposition leader Sali Berisha urges Democratic Party supporters and businesses to back the students, and says he is against damaging property. No separate opposition protest has been reported.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: State Police chief Skënder Hita says 167 people have been arrested and 388 others face criminal proceedings over five days of protests, 132 officers have been injured and seven officers suspended pending disciplinary investigations. He says online groups are calling for violence against police; he gives no figure for injured protesters.

events.label: reported
events.text: Reuters says its video shows police firing a shotgun towards crowds outside the Education Ministry, that its reporters found rubber pellets on the ground, and that pellets hit two Reuters journalists and several protesters. Police chief Hita does not deny using rubber bullets and says the means were used in a limited way.

events.label: reported
events.text: Rama visits businesses damaged in the unrest, warns against further destruction and accuses his conservative opponents of encouraging the violence, AFP and AP report (via Al Jazeera).

events.label: reported
events.text: The health ministry says nine protesters and four police officers received medical treatment on Saturday, AFP and AP report (via Al Jazeera).

events.label: reported
events.text: News24 reports that President Bajram Begaj has met two groups of protesters on separate days; they asked him to dissolve parliament and set up a one-year transitional government to prepare early elections. No statement from the president's office has been reported.

events.label: reported
events.text: The US Embassy in Tirana calls on all sides to show restraint and keep calm, saying citizens should protest peacefully and that violence and destruction of property are not civic engagement, Gazeta Shqiptare reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Protests continue into Saturday night; the Supreme Court building, the entrance of the Bank of Albania, banks and a post office are set on fire or badly damaged, AFP reports. Justice Minister Toni Gogu says the attacks targeted independent institutions, not the government.

events.label: reported
events.text: AFP reports that the health ministry says 35 people were injured on Saturday, 18 police officers and 17 protesters, a higher figure than the ministry gave earlier in the day.

events.label: alleged
events.text: In a live video on Sunday morning, Prime Minister Edi Rama says police neutralised a drone carrying explosives two days earlier that was meant to hit the Prime Minister's Office, and says a foreign hand, not students, is behind the violence, Euronews Albania and Koha report. No police statement or evidence about the drone has been reported.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Albania's health ministry says 272 people have been injured since the protests began on October 14, including 169 police officers, Al Jazeera and Srpske Novine report; Srpske Novine breaks the figure down further as 169 police, 82 demonstrators and 21 passers-by.

events.label: reported
events.text: A Sunday-morning health ministry report put the day's injuries at 65, including 37 police officers with 12 hospitalised, Al Jazeera reports; Euronews cites an earlier ministry update putting Sunday's toll at 28 injured, including 19 police, a discrepancy consistent with the ministry revising figures through the day.

events.label: reported
events.text: A police station is set on fire and the entrance to the interior ministry is damaged by fire during Sunday's clashes; windows are also smashed at the ruling Socialist Party's headquarters, Euronews and AFP (via Daily Sabah) report.

events.label: reported
events.text: Rama repeats that he will not resign, says his government "is not being challenged," and says those responsible for property damage must be held accountable, Al Jazeera reports.

events.label: disputed
events.text: Injury totals differ: the health ministry's cumulative figure is 272 since the protests began (per Al Jazeera and Srpske Novine), while AFP separately reports about 300 people injured in the clashes overall, more than half of them police.

events.label: reported
events.text: A small group smashes the doors and windows of the Appeals Tribunal in Tirana on Monday afternoon before police intervene; clashes also flare outside the Education Ministry, with protesters throwing stones and police responding with tear gas, AFP (via Daily Sabah) reports.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Rama says on Facebook that demonstrators have crossed a "red line," writing that "protests are a right, whereas violence is a crime," and says he is open to dialogue except with those who commit violence. He pledges a one-off €2,500 payment to frontline police and a "significant" salary increase from January 1, and blames "foreign hands" for the unrest, naming Iran and Russia as sources of online disinformation and alleging tens of thousands of fake profiles tied to Iran, AFP (via Daily Sabah) and Euronews report.

events.label: reported
events.text: Police spokesman Albert Nushi condemns the attack on the police station, saying "an attack on a police station is not a protest," and urges peaceful demonstrators to stay away from masked individuals. The European Commission condemns the violence and says any police response must remain proportionate, Euronews reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Ombudsman's National Mechanism for the Prevention of Torture, led by commissioner Ahmet Prençi, presents preliminary findings saying overcrowding and shortages of beds, water, heating and medical care threatened detainees' rights. It says 11 people, including eight minors held at Police Station No. 1, complained of physical or verbal abuse, with signs of injury found on two of them, and that officers at two stations wore no visible identification numbers. It recommends visible police ID, cameras in interview rooms and child-sensitive procedures, and says it will monitor compliance; no police response has been reported, inAlbania.info reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Rama renews his offer to meet protesters “anytime, anywhere, without conditions,” urging organisers to keep minors out of clashes and distance themselves from violence; he again rules out resigning or negotiating with anyone involved in violence. Police say five people have been arrested and 15 others are being sought, Anadolu Agency (via Anews) reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Speaking at the education ministry, Rama holds up a stone to argue thrown objects can become weapons, separates violence from the right to protest, and calls the unrest “hybrid warfare” fuelled by genuine grievances over housing and jobs; he repeats unproven claims that some media outlets and unnamed foreign actors have a financial and political interest in stoking the unrest. He renews his dialogue offer and places chairs outside his office, which protesters overturn and damage while continuing to demand his resignation. University lecturers and parents join the protests, and the SPUSH academic staff union marches from Tirana Polytechnic University to the prime minister's office over separate pay demands dating to March.

events.label: reported
events.text: Speaking to police chiefs, Rama again rules out negotiating with protesters involved in violence, saying “the moment the state negotiates with this, the state has fallen.” The health ministry's injury toll stands at 295, including 186 police officers, before Monday's violence, and rights lawyer Gentian Sejrani says he is now providing legal aid to more than 100 people who have been arrested, The Nation (Pakistan) reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Students reject Rama's dialogue offer, seeing it as an attempt to seat a hand-picked group and end the protests, and university professors say they will not negotiate with the government unless students take part, Albanian Daily News reports. Protesters announce a new rally outside parliament for 9am Thursday.

events.label: reported
events.text: A Tirana court rules that 18 arrests from the protests were unlawful and orders the release of 27 people, rejecting prosecutors' requests to impose security measures on them; nine others are ordered to report periodically to the Judicial Police, and two people whose arrests were ruled lawful must do the same, Albanian Daily News reports, citing the court record. Those involved were accused of organising or taking part in unlawful gatherings, resisting police, or property damage; the published decision gives no reasoning for the unlawful-arrest finding, and no second outlet has reported it yet.

events.label: reported
events.text: Parliamentary leaders reject an opposition request to debate the student protests, now in their tenth day; opposition MPs block the podium and bang on desks while other lawmakers keep voting on legislation, holding up photos of students they say were injured by police in earlier clashes, Euronews reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: In a video message on Friday, Rama calls the protesters "criminals, communists, political opponents" and says enemies in Serbia, Greece, Russia and Iran are stoking the unrest, widening the blame beyond the Iran and Russia claims he made on October 19. He spends part of the video reading out alleged criminal records, without naming them, for men he describes as mostly in their 30s who were arrested over the past ten days, Courthouse News reports.

events.label: pending
events.text: A reconciled arrest and injury total for Saturday's rally, any response from President Begaj to the protesters' demands, evidence for the explosives-laden drone the prime minister says was neutralised, and the outcome of investigations into the people Rama's government has accused of violence. Still being checked.

events.label: reported
events.text: Another mass protest is planned outside the prime minister's building for Saturday, October 24, Courthouse News reports, as the movement enters its twelfth day.

events.label: reported
events.text: Demonstrators reject Prime Minister Rama's offer of dialogue at Saturday's rally outside his office in Tirana, overturning concrete blocks painted with the word "dialogue"; medical students and healthcare workers join the protest, TVP World reports.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Trade unions, university lecturers, doctors and a cultural workers' union join Saturday's rally outside the prime minister's office in Tirana, alongside students from other cities and members of Albania's diaspora, Albanian Daily News and Albeu.com report. The opposition Democratic Party also urges its members to support the demonstration.

events.label: reported
events.text: Protesters set rubbish bins alight and throw stones at police outside the Education Ministry on Durrës Street in Tirana, prompting officers to fire water cannon and tear gas, Albanian Daily News reports. The clash comes as Saturday's day-12 rally continues outside the prime minister's office; no injuries or arrests have been reported yet.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Democratic Party supporters gather outside the prime minister's office and set fire to pillows Rama had placed there as a symbolic invitation to dialogue, before moving to join the student protest at the Education Ministry. With about 2,500 officers deployed in Tirana, police use tear gas, water cannon and rubber bullets; some protesters throw stones and roll burning bins at the ministry, and several government buildings are attacked. Authorities say more than 300 protesters and police have been injured and dozens of demonstrators have been detained, Al Jazeera and Euronews report.

events.label: reported
events.text: Rama says the state's response to the violence will be "prolonged and persistent" and that authorities have published images and details of dozens of people they accuse of involvement in the violence; he renews his call for the heads of several public institutions to resign. He again blames "foreign actors", accusing Russia and Iran of spreading online misinformation, and repeats his call for dialogue, Euronews reports; Al Jazeera separately reports Rama blamed foreign actors for the violence. Demonstrators' demands include Rama's resignation, better support for education and action on corruption and the cost of living.

events.label: reported
events.text: Prime Minister Edi Rama has announced plans for tougher legislation on demonstrations, including fines, penalties for violent protesters, and the removal of social media posts calling for violence, TRT World reports.

claims.title: Who is behind the violence?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: Rama says the unrest is not a student phenomenon and blames foreign hands and the opposition, which he says is using masked people. Police urge peaceful protesters to distance themselves from masked agitators.
claims.b: Students say they are protesting university conditions, costs and job prospects after months of ignored peaceful protest. Opposition leader Sali Berisha denies the opposition is involved in the violence.
claims.status: Open. Neither side has published evidence; police investigations are under way.

claims.title: Has police force been proportionate?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: Police say anyone who uses violence, burns property or attacks officers bears individual responsibility, and report officers injured by stones, hard objects and explosives.
claims.b: Organisers allege excessive police violence against protesters and journalists. A trauma hospital official attributed a 19-year-old's broken leg to police violence, and the Association of Albanian Journalists condemned police obstruction of reporters.
claims.status: Five officers suspended and an investigation opened by the Police Supervision Agency with prosecutors (OBCT, October 13).

claims.title: Should the Zvërnec resort go ahead?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: Rama says the project will go ahead and be completed responsibly; OSW, a Polish research centre, reports that he says it will create 10,000 jobs.
claims.b: Protesters say the plans lack transparency and threaten a protected wetland home to flamingos and other wildlife.
claims.status: Planning permission has been granted but full details have not been published, according to OSW. Cost estimates differ: about €5 billion (Reuters) and at least $1.4 billion (OSW). Reuters found no evidence of wrongdoing by Kushner.
